answer: Reputation-weighted transaction fee. Each identity's fee multiplier rises with the number of near-identical behavior clones detected, forming an accelerating ridge of marginal cost per additional identity. A small ripple of cloned activity raises the next clone's fee sharply, so N clones cost the attacker roughly N-squared in total fees. Fees also scale with graph overlap: shared counterparties add a timber penalty per link. An attacker pays superlinear fees per identity until clustering costs exceed the value of the marginal clone.
